title: Empiric Antibiotics — Community-Acquired Pneumonia
sources: IDSA 2025 position statement on the ATS CAP update

changelog.change: Initial entry — syndrome structure only. Drug/dose selection must reflect the local antibiogram. Non-severe CAP timing defers to local protocol per the live IDSA/ATS disagreement.

summary: Syndrome-level structure for CAP. Drug and dose choices are intentionally NOT hardcoded — they must reflect your institution's current antibiogram and IDSA updates.

body.text: The decision to initiate empiric antibiotics in non-severe CAP should be made at the local level, per institutional protocol. IDSA declined to endorse the 2025 ATS CAP update; the two societies disagree specifically on timing/threshold for empiric antibiotics in NON-SEVERE CAP. They agree that severe CAP should be treated promptly.
Severe CAP (both societies agree — treat promptly)

Criteria: septic shock requiring vasopressors, or respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation, or ≥ 3 minor criteria (RR ≥ 30, PaO₂/FiO₂ ≤ 250, multilobar infiltrates, confusion, uremia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, hypothermia, hypotension needing aggressive fluids). Empiric coverage class: a beta-lactam + a macrolide OR a beta-lactam + a respiratory fluoroquinolone; add MRSA and/or antipseudomonal coverage if risk factors are present (prior isolation, recent hospitalization + IV antibiotics, local prevalence). Pick the specific agents/doses from your antibiogram.

items: Outpatient, no comorbidities / risk factors: coverage class — amoxicillin (high-dose) OR doxycycline OR a macrolide where local pneumococcal resistance is low
Outpatient with comorbidities, or inpatient (non-ICU): a beta-lactam + a macrolide, OR a respiratory fluoroquinolone alone
Timing of the first dose: per local protocol (see the callout above)

body.text: Minimum 5 days AND clinically stable (afebrile ≥ 48 h, haemodynamically stable, able to maintain oral intake, normal mentation) before stopping. De-escalate to targeted therapy once cultures return. Do not routinely add anaerobic coverage for aspiration pneumonitis.

buildNote: Tier 3 / institution-specific. Structure the module so the syndrome categories are stable but the drug rows are editable content that gets refreshed against the antibiogram. HAP/VAP, UTI, intra-abdominal, SSTI, meningitis, and sepsis-of-unknown-source now live in the empiric-antibiotics-ed-icu module, built on this same pattern.
